issues.title: Managed Home-button state is exposed through editable customization controls
issues.component: Desktop toolbar context menu and Customize Toolbar policy metadata
steps: Proposed, not executed: in an isolated test profile, set mandatory ShowHomeButton=true and call CustomizeToolbarHandler::ListActions(). Inspect Home's management field and effective pin state.
Construct the Home context-menu model in a regular profile and inspect Unpin enablement. Activate it and compare the effective preference and visibility with the requested user value.
Repeat mandatory ShowHomeButton=false through Customize Toolbar; use recommended true as the editable control case.
After source-level assertions are validated, use an authorized disposable runtime profile to inspect keyboard activation and announcements.
issues.expected: The management field should describe the effective policy-controlled Home state, and pin/unpin controls should reflect preference modifiability while preserving recommended-policy editability.
issues.observed: At the pinned revision, ListActions reads Home's effective preference but supplies false for its enterprise-controlled field. The WebUI chooses an editable row when that field is false. Native pin/unpin enablement checks regular-profile status and pinnability, and preference-backed Home is treated as pinnable without checking policy management. SetBoolean writes the user store, which remains lower priority than mandatory managed values.
issues.inferredFailureScenario: Mandatory true can leave an enabled Unpin command and editable Home toggle that write a shadowed user value while effective visibility remains policy-controlled. Mandatory false similarly exposes an editable Customize Toolbar toggle. The exact visible or announced effect was not observed.
issues.confirmationScope: Source-confirmed metadata/enablement inconsistency only; no policy bypass or local runtime defect is established.

codeEvidence.observation: This entry maps ShowHomeButton to prefs::kShowHomeButton as a boolean.
The effective Home preference is followed by an unconditional false management field.
The interface explicitly defines whether the pinned state is currently enterprise controlled.
False selects the clickable row/cr-toggle branch; the other branch displays managed explanatory text.
Home wires the shared pinned-action context-menu model with kActionHome.
The pin/unpin branch omits a preference-management check.
Home belongs to the preference-backed pin-state group and maps to kShowHomeButton.
Preference-backed actions satisfy IsPinnable and write their preference on activation.
SetBoolean delegates to a user-preference write.
The write targets the user store rather than mandatory managed values.
Mandatory managed values precede user values in the highest-to-lowest priority enum.
Effective-value lookup selects the first matching non-default store in priority order.

vendorStatements.statement: The checked-in policy description says a configured policy determines Home-button visibility and users cannot change it; the definition also advertises recommended-policy support. This describes intended semantics, not measured UX.

existingTests.observation: Tests ordinary pin/unpin visibility and writes without setting policy management.

duplicateLookup.outcome: No exact duplicate verified in the completed free-search queries.
duplicateLookup.boundary: Search results and the selected test files do not establish repository-wide test absence or issue novelty.

recommendationCandidates: Expose authoritative management and effective pin state, and gate native pin/unpin on preference modifiability while preserving recommended-policy editability.
Represent a managed-off Home setting with accurate locked-off wording instead of blindly reusing the existing enterprise-enabled branch.

followUpTest.proposal: Add a managed-state Reset test: Reset clears user preferences while IsDefault compares effective values. Reset-button and announcement behavior under policy is an unverified follow-up, not an additional confirmed issue.

limitations: Source-only inconsistency; no browser build, live policy matrix, screen-reader result or test execution was observed.
No policy bypass is claimed: mandatory managed values retain priority over these user-store writes.
No managed-Home coverage was found in the inspected tests; a full repository test search was not performed.
Affected released versions, feature rollout state and exact user-visible behavior are unknown.

submission.reason: Needs isolated validation and a verified duplicate check; no issue was submitted by this project.

issues.title: Toolbar WebUI test fixtures contradict the production data: icon invariant
issues.component: Customize Toolbar WebUI test data contract
steps: Proposed, not executed: verify that the generated resources in an isolated Chromium test build correspond to the pinned revision.
Run the existing --gtest_filter=SidePanelCustomizeChromeTest.Toolbar in its appropriate upstream test binary.
Capture assertion and promise-rejection reporting for tests using createToolbarElementWithBasicData; distinguish a fixture assertion from an end-user product failure.
issues.expected: Normal fixture icons and their expected values should satisfy the production data: URL invariant, so ordinary structure and pinning tests do not introduce an unrelated asynchronous assertion.
issues.observed: The production list-actions callback asserts that each iconUrl starts with data:. The shared WebUI fixture supplies the same HTTPS example icon twice, and the icon test expects that HTTPS URL. The inspected assert implementation throws on false, while the real browser handler encodes PNG data URIs.
issues.inferredFailureScenario: The fixture reaches a false assertion in the asynchronous list-actions callback when using the inspected assertion implementation. Whether the test harness fails, reports an unhandled rejection or uses transformed assertions was not established.
issues.confirmationScope: Source-confirmed fixture/production contract mismatch, not a demonstrated test-run failure or end-user Chrome defect.

codeEvidence.observation: The production callback enforces a data: prefix for every icon URL.
Both basic fixture actions use an HTTPS icon rather than a data URI.
The icon test explicitly depends on the contract-invalid fixture URL.
The inspected assertion implementation throws on a false value.
Real handler output uses data-URI encoding, consistent with the production invariant.

issues.title: A running overflow menu may dispatch a different action after pin-order changes
steps: Proposed, not executed: extend the existing overflow unit fixture with two distinct action labels and callback counters, and mark both actions overflowed.
Create/show the menu and retain action A's displayed label and numeric command ID.
Call MovePinnedAction(B, 0), check whether the old menu survives, then activate the retained command.
Assert that either the old menu was invalidated or the invoked action still matches the retained label.
Only after fixture validation, test a controlled preference update with a real open overflow menu in an authorized disposable runtime profile.
issues.expected: A surviving menu command should continue to identify the action named by its displayed label, or the menu should be invalidated when the mapping changes.
issues.observed: Source inspection shows menu creation using responsive_elements_ indices as stored command IDs and snapshotting labels. OnActionsChanged reorders that vector, while execution resolves an existing numeric command against the current vector. The selected tests cover reordering and activation separately.
issues.inferredFailureScenario: If a menu stays alive while a model update swaps actions A and B, the old command for A can resolve to B while still displaying A's label. Synchronization is a plausible asynchronous trigger, not a demonstrated production path. Automatic menu closure on every relevant update would prevent the proposed user-facing failure.
issues.confidenceBasis: High confidence in the conditional index/label mismatch; only medium confidence in production reachability because whole-UI cancellation behavior was not established.

codeEvidence.observation: Creation stores a responsive-elements index as command ID with the current label; the icon branch also uses i.
This observer reorders the vector without rebuilding the open menu in this method.
Execution resolves the stored numeric command against the current vector.
The model refreshes preference-derived IDs before notifying observers.
Non-dynamic labels and command IDs are retained in the menu model's stored items.
Activation dispatches that stored command ID to the delegate.

issues.title: Actions hidden at first enumeration may miss their first visibility-change notification
steps: Proposed, not executed: in the existing handler browser-test fixture, make DevTools invisible before the first ListActions call.
Enumerate once and clear mock expectations, then set DevTools visible without changing another action, the model or the theme.
Verify a client update followed by DevTools appearing, without an unrelated refresh.
If the fixture shows the missed update, trace a genuine production eligibility transition before escalating a user-facing report.
issues.expected: For a live-updating customization list, an existing action that becomes visible after initial enumeration should trigger a refresh even if it was initially hidden.
issues.observed: ListActions returns for invisible actions before installing their change callbacks. The inspected handler stores per-ID subscriptions and model/preference observations. SetVisible triggers the changed action's callback, and the WebUI repopulates when notified. Existing visibility coverage begins with DevTools visible and already enumerated.
issues.inferredFailureScenario: An initially hidden action becomes visible with no other subscribed action, model or theme event. Its own missed subscription can leave the WebUI omitting it until another refresh. Coupled eligibility or visibility updates may mask this scenario; no production action making the independent transition was traced.
issues.confidenceBasis: High confidence in the hidden-first subscription edge; medium confidence in observable production impact because other notifications can refresh the list.

codeEvidence.observation: The invisible-action early return precedes subscription installation.
Only an action that reaches this block receives the per-ID callback subscription.
Action/model callbacks notify the WebUI; preference callbacks update individual pin state.
The handler owns per-ID action subscriptions plus model and preference observations.
Constructor observation covers the model and three pin preferences, not an action-tree-wide visibility observer.
A changed visible value emits that action's change callback.
The WebUI binds action-update notifications to populateUi_; theme changes also repopulate.

issues.title: Open overflow menu enablement may remain stale while action enablement changes
issues.component: Responsive overflow-menu live enabled and accessible state
steps: Proposed, not executed: show a two-action overflow menu in the existing fixture, with one action enabled and the other disabled.
Change the underlying enabled action with SetEnabled(false) and the other with SetEnabled(true), and first check whether the menu survives or closes.
Compare model enabled state with MenuItemView::GetEnabled() for the surviving menu, then verify keyboard selectability and accessibility state in an authorized runtime test.
Establish whether live enabled-state updates or a deliberately frozen snapshot are intended before labeling the behavior a defect.
issues.expected: If the menu is intended to reflect live action state, its visible, keyboard and accessible enabled state should remain consistent with invocation availability, or it should close when that state becomes invalid. A deliberate snapshot contract must be evaluated separately.
issues.observed: PopulateMenu copies enabled state onto normal MenuItemViews. Its running ActionItemChanged path updates icon color and status-indicator visibility, not label or enabled state. The model's IsCommandIdEnabled reads current state, but the class does not override Views' distinct IsCommandEnabled, whose default is true. ActionItem invocation still refuses disabled execution.
issues.inferredFailureScenario: If the menu stays open, an action that becomes disabled may still appear or announce enabled while activation does nothing; an action that becomes enabled may remain unselectable until reopening. No accessibility tree or runtime event was observed.
issues.confidenceBasis: Concrete partial-update paths support a consistency test, but menu cancellation and the intended live-state contract were not established.

codeEvidence.observation: Menu population copies current enabled state onto each normal view.
The running-menu callback changes indicator visibility and icon color; its inspected body contains no enabled-state or label refresh.
The model delegate queries enabled state when asked.
The class overrides the model delegate's IsCommandIdEnabled, not Views' differently named IsCommandEnabled.
Views' default command-enabled response is true.
Changing ActionItem enablement emits a change notification.
InvokeAction retains its enabled guard; this hypothesis does not claim an authorization bypass.
The controller delegates action-ID enablement to the current ActionItem.
Model IsEnabledAt consults the delegate as well as the stored item's enabled flag.

existingTests.observation: Establishes enabled/disabled states before showing the menu and checks the model.

existingTests.name: OverflowMenuTest.StatusIndicatorVisibilityUpdates
existingTests.observation: Changes live underline-indicator state rather than live enablement.

duplicateLookup.outcome: Shared overflow searches and the dedicated disabled-state query did not verify this exact scenario.
duplicateLookup.boundary: Returned extension-menu, fullscreen and historical HiDPI snippets were not verified issue bodies. Issue status, exhaustive coverage and novelty remain unknown.

recommendationCandidates: If the mismatch is reproduced and conflicts with the intended contract, refresh enabled and accessible state on action changes or close the menu consistently.
Validate keyboard/accessibility state together with visual state rather than updating indicators alone.
limitations: A deliberately frozen menu snapshot may be intentional; this has not been labeled a confirmed defect.
Menu survival, keyboard selectability and accessibility state were not measured.
The ActionItem execution guard remains, so no authorization bypass is established.
Only selected tests were inspected; duplicate coverage and released-version impact are incomplete.

submission.reason: Needs a surviving-menu reproduction and confirmation of the intended live-state behavior before escalation.
